extracted.intended_audience: editors, indexers, book and journal publishers, and authors preparing manuscripts and indexes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing, editing, and formatting manuscripts, indexes, journal articles, and related front/back matter for publication. Covers indexing mechanics, punctuation, formatting (italics, initialisms), journal metadata, and proofreading/production requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index entries — locators and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Locators: appropriate use of; chapternumbers with; checking; ff and et seq. not appropriate with; italics and boldface for; long strings of; pagination final for; paragraph numbers as; number per entry; number per page; page ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance emphasizes careful checking of locators (16.12; 16.111; 16.133), avoiding ff and et seq., appropriate typographic treatments (italics/boldface 16.116,16.140–143), limits on numbers per entry/page, using paragraph numbers as locators (1.125,2.106,16.12,16.13,16.108), and attention to page ranges and final pagination (2.104–6,2.113,2.118,16.108).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main headings in indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and use of main headings; alphabetizing of main headings; initial lowercase letters; inversion in main headings; noun or noun phrase recommended; refining terms; vs. subentries; typing and modifying; undifferentiated locators after main headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main headings should generally be a noun or noun phrase (16.9), may use inversion (16.9,16.56,16.94), begin with initial lowercase where appropriate (16.11), be alphabetized (16.56), refined as needed (16.126), and handled consistently with subentries (16.127).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation in indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for punctuation in indexes including colons, em dashes, en dashes; punctuation with locators; punctuation in indented and run-in styles; punctuation for subentries and sub-subentries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific cross-references: colons (16.19–20,16.25,16.95), em dashes (6.92,16.27,16.99,16.141), en dashes (16.100,16.111,16.134). Punctuation interacts with style (indented vs run-in) and with locators (16.94–100,16.25–28,16.95–96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subentries — when and how to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and use of subentries; alphabetizing subentries; handling articles in subentries; chronological vs numerical order; cross-references in/for subentries; excessive numbers; indentation and syntax; run-in vs indented style; punctuation and marking proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subentries judiciously (16.10,16.120–128); alphabetize them (16.68–70); decide on articles treatment (16.51–52,16.68); choose chronological or numerical order where appropriate (16.70,16.69); set indentation and punctuation consistently (16.95–96,16.137); mark proofs and check for excessive subentries (16.117–21,16.133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-subentries and deeper levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid sub-subentries where possible; rules for continued lines, punctuation, indented vs run-in style, and syntax for sub-subentries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance recommends avoiding deep nesting (16.27,16.133). If used, follow specific formatting and punctuation rules (16.27–28,16.99,16.142–43) and manage continued lines (16.139).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes — general format and style choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Choices between indented (hanging/flush-and-hang) and run-in styles; continued lines; cross-references; headnotes; hanging indentation; submission format; placement in book; table-of-contents inclusion; running heads; indented vs run-in guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed descriptions and examples for indented style (16.26,16.28,16.142–43) and run-in style (16.25,16.27,16.141), plus guidance on headnotes (16.116,16.140–145), hanging indentation (16.24,16.106,16.131), submission format (16.131), and placement (1.4,1.65).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic index generation discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic 'generation' not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexes require human editorial decisions and cannot be reliably generated automatically (16.105).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing, checking, and proofreading indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing of indexes: checking cross-references; editing and refining entries; checking main headings; marking proofs; noting errors in text; pagination final; proofreading responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing requires multiple checks (16.124–33): refine terms, check cross-references (16.17–20,16.26), mark proofs carefully (16.117–21), verify final pagination (2.104–6,2.113,2.118,16.108), and correct text errors (16.125,16.131).

rubrics_metrics.name: Index length and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on length of indexes, number per page, limits on long strings of locators, excessive subentries, and overall quality considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider length limits and publisher preferences (16.103,16.118,16.133), control long locator strings (16.120,16.128,16.133), avoid excessive subentries (16.133), and target index quality (16.132).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of indexes and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Types include single vs multiple indexes, author-and-title (for anthologies), authors' names index, first-lines, embedded, hyperlinked/online indexes; order of multiple indexes; separate vs consecutive pagination in multivolume works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose index types appropriate to work (16.6; 16.7; 1.9), plan order of multiple indexes (1.65), and handle multivolume pagination carefully (1.9). Online/hyperlinked indexes have special considerations (1.125,16.7,16.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic considerations for indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Address bad breaks, continued lines, distinguishing types of entries and locators, justification, typesetting instructions, type size, and column width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to typographic problems (16.138–39), ensure clarity in distinguishing entry types and locators (16.116,16.140–43), and specify typesetting instructions including column width and type size (16.134,1.65,16.135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing names — personal and place names
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for indexing personal names: academic titles and offices, compound names, initials and hyphens, Jr./Sr./III, Mac/Mc/O’, married women’s names, unfamiliar forms, variants, and entities with same name; place-names rules and definite article handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific rules for names (16.71–75,16.72,16.40–43,16.33,16.62,16.64,16.37,16.90–93). Treat non-English names, pseudonyms, and variants with care; manage identical names (16.35,16.62).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexer vs. author responsibilities and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Author's role in supplying terms for indexer; responsibility for indexes; professional indexers vs software; preparation and submission schedule; editing someone else's index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify responsibilities: authors may supply terms (16.34), but professional indexers often produce the index (16.3–4); provide materials early (16.101–8), use software as an aid (16.5,16.104), and follow publisher schedules (16.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Index submission and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission format for indexes; marking proofs; typing and modifying entries; marking continued lines and runover lines; checking of main headings; publisher preferences for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow submission specs (16.131), mark proofs carefully (16.117–21), adhere to publisher preferences (16.103,16.106,16.118,16.123,16.129), and prepare index text for typesetting (16.122–23,16.134).

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics — uses and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Italic use defined and common uses: titles of works, emphasis, non-English terms, scientific names, epigraphs, stage directions, mathematical copy, notes keyed by page numbers, and more; marking manuscripts and proofs for italics; punctuation and italics interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific uses and interactions (8.173; 7.48; 14.60; 8.2; 13.36; 12.10; 14.53). Mark italic text in manuscripts (2.73,2.97) and proofs (2.131), mind punctuation and possessives in italics (6.2; 7.29), and consider semantic markup notes (2.82n1,7.49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialisms and initials — formatting and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and use of initialisms; capitalization; spacing; ampersand use; articles with initialisms; possessives of initialisms; small vs full-size capitals; indexing of initialisms and initials; punctuation and spacing of initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow rules for capitals and spacing (10.2; 10.5–10.12), ampersand rules (10.10), possessives (7.17), indexing treatment (16.49,16.64), and punctuation/spacing in source citations (14.73–74,15.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal article metadata and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for journal articles: abstracts, authors' names as metadata, access dates, continuous publishing model, page ranges and page numbering, first-page information, hyperlinks and electronic supplementary data, submission and publication dates, DOIs and URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide abstracts and keywords (1.92–95;1.93), include metadata (1.92,1.100), record access dates (14.176), handle continuous publishing (1.82;14.174), and include DOIs/URLs where applicable (1.79;14.23;14.175).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals — components, house style, and production
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals comprise front matter, articles, indexes, abstracts, table of contents, editorial policy, peer review, publishing agreements, ISSN/ISBN metadata, production schedule, proofs, and open-access considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow house style (1.108–9;14.2–4), manage peer review and editorial processes (2.5;1.84–86), include required metadata and identifiers (1.79–86,1.92), prepare production schedules and proofs (2.102;2.134), and account for open-access licenses (4.61–62).

rubrics_metrics.name: ISBN and ISSN usage and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement of ISBN on copyright page and covers; ISBNs for e-books and multiple formats; ISBN Agency guidance; ISSN usage for serials and metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ISBN on copyright page and covers (1.20,1.32,1.74; fig.1.1, fig.1.4), manage ISBNs for multiple formats (1.20,1.32,4.64), consult ISBN Agency resources (1.32), and use ISSN for serial metadata (1.20,1.79–86,1.92,1.103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line spacing and manuscript submission formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for line spacing in manuscript editing and submission; spacing between paragraphs and stanzas; word-processing styles; electronic file cleanup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify line spacing for submissions and editing (2.6,2.8,2.19–24,2.91), use consistent spacing between paragraphs and quoted stanzas (13.22–25), employ word-processing styles (2.82), and clean up electronic files (2.80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line breaks and nonbreaking conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling line breaks with em dashes/en dashes, nonbreaking spaces, slashes, URLs, numbers, and proper names; considerations for reflowable electronic formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inappropriate breaks around dashes (6.90,6.82), use nonbreaking spaces for control (6.11,6.119,6.121), and manage URLs and reflowable formats to prevent bad breaks (2.13;6.113;7.36;14.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels, captions, and keys in illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish labels from captions; capitalization and consistency in keys; scaling and placement; marking submitted artwork for redrawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat labels vs captions distinctly (3.21), keep capitalization consistent in keys (3.20), scale labels appropriately (3.19), and mark submitted art for redrawing as needed (3.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual property rights: originality, reproduction and distribution, public display, derivative works and performance, subdivision of rights, and trademark protection; handling permissions and subsidiary rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish basic vs subsidiary rights (4.17–18), manage permissions for reproduction/distribution and public display (4.13–14,4.34,4.51,4.64,4.76), consider derivatives and performance rights (4.14), and coordinate trademark protection (4.16).
